differential_distribution_table.random_permutation_reference_expected_ma: ~ a few (typically 4-10 for a random 8-bit permutation; textbook AES S-box max is 4/256=0.0156)
differential_distribution_table.note: Lower max differential probability is generally considered better against differential cryptanalysis OF THE S-BOX IN ISOLATION. This does NOT by itself establish anything about the resistance of the FULL cipher (permutation + chained diffusion + key schedule) to differential cryptanalysis -- the S-box here is also DIFFERENT for every (key, nonce), unlike AES's fixed public S-box, which changes the relevant threat model entirely (see final report).

linear_approximation_table.random_permutation_reference: a random 8-bit permutation typically has max|bias| well above textbook-S-box values (e.g. AES S-box's max bias count is 32/256=0.125 in the +-1 convention used here, before any correction factor); exact comparison convention-dependent -- reported here for THIS S-box only, not compared to a freshly-generated random-permutation ensemble average (out of scope at P1 time budget; flagged as a possible follow-on in section 18/limitations).

cross_nonce_sbox_similarity.expected_agreement_for_independent_rando: ~1 (E[agreements]=1, same reasoning as fixed points of a random permutation applied to comparing two independent random permutations)
cross_nonce_sbox_similarity.conclusion: No detected similarity beyond chance between S-boxes derived under different nonces (same key) at this single-sample check.
